destination.name: Tanzania
destination.pitch: The northern circuit is the best concentration of large animals left on earth and it is priced accordingly, with about half your daily spend going to the government before anyone feeds you; Zanzibar afterwards is the part where you stop set

because.nature: Ngorongoro holds black rhino at the best odds in Africa, the Serengeti carries roughly 1.3 million wildebeest and the lion density to match, and Tarangire in the dry season has more elephant per square kilometre than anywhere in the north.
because.exploration: Four ecosystems in a week of driving: baobab savannah, a 600 metre volcanic caldera, open short-grass plain, and then a Swahili trading port on a coral island that had nothing to do with any of it.
because.food: Stone Town eats properly, between Lukmaan's trays and the Emerson rooftops, and Arusha has two or three real restaurants; on safari you eat the camp buffet at the hour the camp serves it and that is the whole story.
because.relaxation: The Zanzibar east coast is a flat reef lagoon where the tide runs the day and three nights of doing nothing is the correct correction to a week of dawn starts.
because.culture: Maasai in the highlands and a thousand years of Omani, Persian and Indian trade in Stone Town, both of which are easy to visit badly, so choose village-run programmes over roadside boma stops.
because.adventure: Walking with an armed ranger is legal in Tarangire, Arusha National Park and the Ngorongoro highlands but not in the Serengeti or the crater, and Paje has the steadiest kite wind in East Africa.
because.city: Arusha is a functional safari town with a market, two small museums and a good dinner, not a place to spend days.

destination.caveat: Park fees alone run USD 53 to 83 per person per day plus a USD 348 vehicle charge to descend into the Ngorongoro crater, the migration is a rainfall-driven guess that no operator can promise you on a given date, and driving Arusha to Serengeti is five to eight hours of corrugated road each way unles Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: Arusha
cities.base: Along Baraa or Moivaro Road on the eastern edge, or on a coffee estate off the Dodoma road to the west. Both put you 25 minutes from Arusha Airport, where the light aircraft leave, and out of the town

cities.name: Tarangire National Park
cities.base: Inside the park on the river bluff, at Tarangire Safari Lodge or one of the tented camps, if you want to be on the Tarangire River at first light. Outside the eastern boundary in Randilen if you want

cities.name: Lake Manyara National Park
cities.base: There are lodges on the escarpment and in Mto wa Mbu, but the park is 330 square kilometres of which two thirds is water, and half a day does it. Take it as a morning out of Karatu on the way up to Ng

cities.name: Ngorongoro
cities.base: On the southern crater rim between Seneto and Lemala if the crater is the point: you are at the descent gate at 06:00 rather than driving up from Karatu in the dark, and the rim is cold enough at 2,30

cities.name: Serengeti National Park
cities.base: Follow the grass, not the map. Seronera in the centre for year-round resident game and the shortest transfers, Ndutu in the south from January to March for the calving, Kogatende in the north from lat

cities.name: Stone Town, Zanzibar
cities.base: Inside the old town between Shangani and Mkunazini, which is the only way to see it, because the lanes are too narrow for cars and everything is a seven minute walk. The seafront hotels in Shangani ge

cities.name: Zanzibar east coast
cities.base: Paje if you want to be able to walk to food, a coffee and a kite school, Jambiani 15 minutes south if you want a quieter village and the same lagoon, Michamvi on the peninsula if you want a pool and n

outings.name: The Ngorongoro crater floor day
outings.why: Down the Seneto road at 06:00, the floor until early afternoon, up the Lemala road. Black rhino, the big-tusked Lerai bulls and lion at a density nowhere else matches, shared with a hundred other vehicles on a 260 square kilometre floor. Fr
outings.season: All year. The rim is cloud-locked in the mornings from March
outings.fallback: The rim road east to Sopa and on to Nainokanoka, which gives you the crater from above and the Maasai grazing highlands, for the conservation fee alone.

outings.name: The Seronera river drive
outings.why: Out at 06:00 along the permanent water in the centre of the park, back for a late breakfast. Resident lion prides and the best leopard odds in Tanzania, and also the busiest tracks in the park, so a good sighting means ten vehicles.
outings.fallback: The Serengeti Visitor Centre kopje trail and the Retima hippo pool, both of which work in rain when the black cotton tracks do not.

outings.name: The Mara River crossing wait at Kogatende
outings.why: You drive to a crossing point, park, and wait. Herds gather, walk to the bank, turn around and do it again, sometimes for hours, sometimes all day, sometimes not at all. It is the single most oversold thing in East African travel and also,
outings.season: Late July to late October, peaking August and September, and
outings.fallback: The Mara River hippo pools and the Lamai wedge resident game, which are there whether or not the wildebeest are.

outings.name: The Ndutu calving plains
outings.why: Short grass, half a million wildebeest, and the three weeks in February when most of the calves drop. Cheetah hunt on open ground here in daylight, which is the reason to come. Ndutu is inside the conservation area, so it is an NCA permit r
outings.season: December to March, with the calving peak in early to mid Feb
outings.fallback: The Naabi Hill and Gol kopjes circuit on the park side, for cheetah on the plains without the crowding at the calving grounds.

outings.name: The Silale swamp loop in Tarangire
outings.why: Two hours south on rough track to the permanent swamps, lunch in the vehicle, two hours back. The lion prides and the big elephant bulls are down here, and almost nobody on a three day circuit comes this far. After rain the black cotton soi
outings.season: Best June to October. Difficult or impossible in March to Ma
outings.fallback: The Tarangire River circuit from the gate to Kuro and back, on better track, with the lodge terrace for lunch.

outings.name: The Tarangire river circuit
outings.why: Gate at 06:00, down the sand river past the baobabs to Matete and back by late morning. In the dry months this is the highest elephant density in northern Tanzania. In the green months the herds leave the park entirely and this is a pleasan
outings.season: All year, transformed from June to October
outings.fallback: The Lemiyon baobab plain just inside the gate, which is ten minutes from the fee desk and holds game even when the river is quiet.

outings.name: The Empakaai crater rim to lake walk
outings.why: Two hours of bad road north from the crater rim, then a steep 300 metre drop through forest to a flamingo lake and the same climb back out at 2,600 metres. A compulsory ranger and a walking fee of about USD 24. You will see Maasai herders a
outings.season: All year. The descent is slippery and sometimes closed after
outings.fallback: Olmoti Crater and the Munge waterfall from Nainokanoka, a shorter walk on the same permit.

outings.name: The dawn balloon over the Seronera valley

startsFrom.name: Camps within 45 minutes of Seronera airstrip

outings.why: Pickup at 04:30, airborne at first light for an hour, champagne breakfast on the grass afterwards, back at camp by 10:00. Around USD 599 to 650 per person. Cancelled outright for wind, with a refund rather than a second attempt, so book it
outings.fallback: A normal 06:00 game drive on the Seronera circuit, which costs nothing extra and often sees more.

outings.name: The Olduvai Gorge stop on the Ngorongoro to Serengeti road
outings.why: The museum rebuilt in 2017 sits directly on the transfer road, so it costs you an hour and a half rather than a day. Laetoli footprint casts, the Leakey excavation story and a terrace over the gorge. About USD 35 per adult on top of the con
outings.fallback: The Maasai grazing plains and the Shifting Sands dune west of the museum, if the museum is closed for an event.

outings.name: The Lake Manyara morning out of Karatu
outings.why: Forty minutes down the escarpment, gate at 06:30, the groundwater forest and the lake shore until late morning, then the village at Mto wa Mbu. Park fee is USD 53.10 to 59 per adult. The tree-climbing lions are real and you will almost cert
outings.season: All year. Best for birds November to May, best for mammals J
outings.fallback: The Mto wa Mbu village walk and the escarpment viewpoint, which need no park ticket at all.

outings.name: The Stone Town walking morning
outings.why: Slave chambers under the cathedral, Darajani market, the carved doors, the Old Fort and the Old Dispensary, all inside a square kilometre on foot. Start at 08:00 for the market and the heat. You will get lost, which is the correct outcome,
outings.season: All year. Avoid the middle of the day from December to March
outings.fallback: The seafront from Forodhani to the Old Dispensary and back, which is shaded and flat.

outings.name: The Jozani forest and the Michamvi peninsula run
outings.why: Red colobus at Jozani by 08:30 while they are still moving, the mangrove boardwalk, then north for lunch at the Rock on a rising tide and the sunset at Kae Funk. Roughly USD 10 for Jozani plus taxi time; the Rock needs booking weeks ahead a
outings.season: All year. The long rains in April and May close a lot of the
outings.fallback: Jozani in the morning and Kuza Cave at Jambiani in the afternoon, both close and both unaffected by tides.

places.name: Cultural Heritage Centre
places.note: Four floors of carving, Tinga Tinga canvases and a tanzanite counter, all at fixed prices well above the curio market. Useful for the half day between a safari landing and a flight out, not much else.

places.name: Natural History Museum at the Old Boma
places.note: The 1900 German fort is the exhibit; the hominid casts and the colonial-era photographs inside are thin and badly lit. Forty minutes is plenty.

places.name: Arusha Declaration Museum
places.neighborhood: Kaloleni, by the Uhuru monument roundabout
places.note: Where Nyerere's 1967 socialist programme is explained on its own terms, which you will not get anywhere else. Small, dated, and worth an hour if you want any political context at all.

places.name: Central Market, Soko Kuu
places.note: A working produce market, not a craft market: dried dagaa, sacks of cardamom, secondhand clothes. Go before 10:00, keep your phone away, and expect to be walked through by someone who will want paying.

places.name: Maasai Curio Market
places.neighborhood: Fire Road, behind the clock tower
places.note: Beadwork, kangas and carvings in a warren of stalls where the selling is relentless. First price is roughly four times the real one, and nobody minds you walking away.

places.name: The Tanzanite Experience
places.note: A small mine-to-market exhibit above a shop, which is the only place in town that will teach you to tell a real stone from a heat-treated one before you spend money. Closed Sundays and it shuts at lunchtime on Saturday.

places.name: Shanga at Arusha Coffee Lodge
places.neighborhood: Burka coffee estate, on the Dodoma road
places.note: A glass and bead workshop employing deaf and disabled Tanzanian artisans, set in a working coffee estate. You watch people blow recycled bottles into glassware, which is more interesting than the shop that follows.

places.name: Africafe
places.note: Arusha coffee roasted in Arusha, proper flat whites, air conditioning and reliable wifi. It is where every safari briefing in town seems to happen.

places.name: Khan's Barbecue
places.note: An auto spares shop that rolls the grills onto the pavement at dusk and sells mishkaki, chicken and naan until late. Cash, plastic chairs, no menu, and one of the better meals in Arusha.

places.name: Machweo at Onsea House
places.neighborhood: Baraa Road, Onsea hill northeast of town
places.note: Belgian-run set menu on a terrace looking back at Meru, the only genuinely serious cooking in Arusha. Book the same day you land, and budget 25 minutes each way in traffic.

places.name: Momella Lakes, Arusha National Park
places.neighborhood: Arusha National Park, northeast of town
places.note: Seven alkaline lakes you can canoe on and walk beside with an armed ranger, which is legal here and not in Ngorongoro or Serengeti. Park entry is about USD 50 plus walking and canoe fees; Meru is clear before 09:00 and gone by 11:00.

places.name: Ngurdoto Crater rim
places.note: A small forested caldera with buffalo on the floor, viewed from a chain of rim lookouts because vehicles are not allowed down. Included in the park fee, and a decent warm-up for Ngorongoro rather than a substitute.

places.name: Tarangire Main Gate at Kwa Kuchinja
places.neighborhood: Northern boundary, off the Arusha to Dodoma road
places.note: Entry is USD 53.10 per adult in low season and USD 59 in high, per 24 hours, card only at the desk. In July and August the queue at 08:00 costs you the best hour of light, so leave Arusha by 06:00.

places.name: The Tarangire River circuit from the gate to Kuro
places.note: The dry-season spine of the park: elephant families digging in the sand river, baobabs, and the densest game between June and October. In the green months the herds disperse east and this drive can be quiet.

places.name: Silale Swamp
places.neighborhood: Southern park, two hours below the gate
places.note: Black cotton soil, permanent water and the resident lion prides, including the tree-climbing ones people come here hoping for. The track is rough and slow, and after rain a two-wheel-drive day ends in a winch.

places.name: The Lemiyon baobab plain
places.note: Open ground scattered with baobabs, several of them hollowed out by elephants over decades. Best late, when the low sun makes the trunks worth photographing.

places.name: Matete Woodland
places.neighborhood: East bank of the Tarangire River
places.note: Doum palms and sausage trees along the river where leopards spend the day. You will drive it slowly and see nothing four times out of five.

places.name: The terrace at Tarangire Safari Lodge
places.neighborhood: Bluff above the Tarangire River, 10 km inside the gate
places.note: The view down the river bend is the best in the park and non-guests can buy lunch or a cold Kilimanjaro on the terrace. It fills with vehicles between 12:30 and 14:00.

places.name: Lake Burunge
places.note: A shallow soda lake on the park edge with flamingo when the water is right and nothing at all when it is not. Worth the detour only if you are already staying on that side.

places.name: Walking safari from Oliver's Camp
places.neighborhood: Southern park, near the Silale swamp
places.note: Tarangire is one of the few northern parks where guided walking with an armed ranger is permitted, and Asilia's camp has run it longest. You leave at 06:30, cover perhaps 8 km, and see less but understand more.

places.name: Night drive in Randilen Wildlife Management Area
places.neighborhood: Community land on the eastern boundary
places.note: Night driving is banned inside the national park, so the spotlight work happens on Maasai-managed land next door. Genets, civets and the occasional leopard; fees go to the villages that own the land.

places.name: Boundary Hill
places.neighborhood: Eastern boundary above the Silale swamp
places.note: A cliff on the park edge that looks down over the whole swamp system, which is the only place you get a sense of Tarangire's shape. The lodge on top is community-owned and will sell you a drink.

places.name: Lake Manyara Main Gate, Mto wa Mbu
places.neighborhood: Mto wa Mbu, at the foot of the escarpment
places.note: USD 53.10 per adult in low season, USD 59 in high, per 24 hours, card only. The gate opens at 06:00 and the park is small enough that arriving at 10:00 wastes it.

places.name: The groundwater forest inside the gate
places.note: Fig and mahogany fed by springs from the escarpment, full of blue monkey and baboon troops in the first kilometre. It is the one stretch of the park that feels nothing like the rest of the northern circuit.

places.name: The Hippo Pool
places.neighborhood: Where the Simba River meets the lake
places.note: Open ground by the lake edge with hippo, pelican and a lot of buffalo. One of the few spots in the park where you can get out of the vehicle, at a marked viewing area.

places.name: Lake Manyara Treetop Walkway
places.note: 370 metres of suspended bridge through the canopy, around USD 60 to 70 on top of park entry. Genuinely good for birds, and the only thing here you cannot do from a vehicle.

places.name: Maji Moto hot springs
places.neighborhood: Southern shore, an hour below the gate
places.note: Hot springs seeping out at the lake edge, hot enough to cook an egg in. The drive down is long, dusty and largely empty of game, so treat it as a reason to see the southern park rather than a destination.

places.name: Mto wa Mbu village walk and market
places.note: A cultural tourism programme run by the village since the 1990s: banana beer, rice paddies, a Tinga Tinga painting shed, the market. Around USD 20 to 25 per person and the money is split with the village fund.

places.name: The Rift escarpment viewpoint above Mto wa Mbu
places.neighborhood: On the B144 climbing to Karatu
places.note: A pull-in on the tarmac where the whole lake and the wall of the Rift open up below you. Curio sellers will reach the car before you are out of it.

places.name: The terrace at Lake Manyara Serena Safari Lodge
places.note: Perched on the rim with the lake 300 metres below, and open to non-guests for lunch or a drink. The view does the work; the buffet does not.

places.name: Canoeing on Lake Manyara
places.note: Runs only when the lake is high enough, which is roughly November to May and not at all in a dry year. Ask before you build a day around it, because operators sell it whether the water is there or not.

places.name: Lodoare Gate
places.note: USD 70.80 per adult per 24 hours, card only, no cash accepted. The permit is single entry, so leaving the conservation area and coming back the same day means paying twice.

places.name: The crater rim viewpoint above Seneto
places.note: The first time you see the whole 260 square kilometre floor at once, 600 metres below. Cloud sits on the rim until mid-morning in the green season, so an early arrival can show you nothing.

places.name: The Seneto descent road
places.neighborhood: Western rim down to the crater floor
places.note: One-way down only, gate open from 06:00. The crater service fee is USD 295 plus VAT per vehicle, about USD 348, split between whoever is in the car, and it buys one descent per day.

places.name: Lerai Forest
places.note: Yellow fever acacia at the foot of the descent, where the crater's elephant bulls spend their days. They are old, huge-tusked and few, and this is the reliable place for them.

places.name: Lake Magadi on the crater floor
places.note: A shallow soda lake, 1.7 metres at its deepest, pink with lesser flamingo when the water level suits them and bare white when it does not. Nobody can tell you in advance which you will get.

places.name: Gorigor Swamp and the Mandusi rhino ground
places.note: The best odds anywhere in East Africa of seeing black rhino, though usually at 400 metres through binoculars with ten other vehicles alongside. Bring more optics than you think you need.

places.name: Ngoitokitok Springs picnic site
places.note: The only place on the floor you are allowed out of the vehicle, beside a hippo pool, with every crater lunchbox in Tanzania arriving at once. Black kites take food out of raised hands, so eat sitting in the car with the door open.

places.name: The Lemala ascent road
places.neighborhood: Eastern wall up to the rim
places.note: The one-way road out, climbing the eastern wall with the whole floor behind you. Vehicles must be off the floor by mid-afternoon and out of the gate by 18:00.

places.name: Olduvai Gorge Museum
places.neighborhood: On the Serengeti road, 45 minutes past the crater
places.note: Rebuilt in 2017 and much better than the old shed: the Leakey excavations, casts of the Laetoli footprints, and a terrace over the gorge itself. Around USD 35 per adult on top of your conservation fee, and it sits exactly on the drive to Serengeti.

places.name: Empakaai Crater rim to lake
places.neighborhood: Northern highlands, two hours from the crater rim
places.note: A steep 300 metre descent through forest to a soda lake full of flamingo, then the same climb back out at 2,600 metres. The drive there is the hard part: rough, slow, and it eats the morning.

places.name: Olmoti Crater and the Munge waterfall
places.neighborhood: Above Nainokanoka village, north of the rim
places.note: A short guided walk up to a grassy caldera and the waterfall that feeds the Ngorongoro floor. Walking fees are about USD 24 per adult plus a compulsory ranger, and you will meet Maasai herders rather than tourists.

places.name: Lunch and the coffee walk at Gibb's Farm
places.neighborhood: Karatu, on the forest edge below the rim
places.note: A 1929 coffee farm that grows most of what it serves and takes non-resident walk-ins for a farm buffet lunch. Book a day ahead, and add the coffee tour or the elephant caves walk if you have the afternoon.

places.name: Naabi Hill Gate
places.neighborhood: Southeast entrance, on the Ngorongoro road
places.note: USD 70.80 per adult per 24 hours in low season, USD 82.60 in high, card only. While the paperwork is done, walk the marked path up the kopje behind the office for the view over the short-grass plains.

places.name: Serengeti Visitor Centre at Seronera
places.note: A short outdoor interpretive trail through a kopje with hyrax underfoot, a decent explanation of how the migration actually works, and a coffee shop with toilets. The best hour of the middle of the day, when the game has gone flat.

places.name: The Seronera river drive
places.note: The permanent water in the middle of the park, which is why the resident lion prides and one of the densest leopard populations anywhere sit along it year round. It is also the most driven ground in the Serengeti, so expect company at every sighting.

places.name: Retima Hippo Pool
places.neighborhood: Where the Seronera and Orangi rivers meet, 15 km north of Se
places.note: Up to a hundred hippo stacked in one bend, and one of the few places you are permitted out of the vehicle on a marked bank. It smells exactly as bad as that many hippo should.

places.name: Moru Kopjes
places.neighborhood: South-central Serengeti, west of the Seronera road
places.note: Granite islands in the grass, good for lion and cheetah, and the part of the park where the last Serengeti rhino are protected. Farther from the lodges than Seronera and correspondingly emptier.

places.name: The Gong Rock and the Maasai paintings at Moru
places.note: A boulder with worn dimples that rings like a bell when struck, used by Maasai before the park displaced them, and ochre shield paintings on an overhang nearby. Ten minutes of actual human history in 15,000 square kilometres of grass.

places.name: Gol Kopjes
places.note: Scattered rock outcrops on open plain, the most reliable cheetah country in the park, and restricted to a limited number of vehicles. Best from December to April when the plains are green and the herds are on them.

places.name: The Ndutu short-grass plains
places.neighborhood: Southern plains, inside the Ngorongoro Conservation Area
places.note: Where roughly half a million wildebeest calves are born in about three weeks around February, with every predator in the ecosystem waiting. It sits in the conservation area, not the park, so it is a separate NCA permit at USD 70.80 a day.

places.name: The dawn balloon over the Seronera valley
places.note: Serengeti Balloon Safaris and Miracle Experience both fly from here; around USD 599 to 650 per person including the champagne breakfast on landing. Pickup is at 04:30 and it is cancelled outright for wind, with a refund rather than a rebooking.

places.name: The Mara River crossing points at Kogatende
places.neighborhood: Northern Serengeti, on the Kenyan border
places.note: You park above a crossing point and wait, sometimes the whole day, for a herd that may balk twice and walk away. Late July to October is the window; anyone promising you a crossing on a given date is guessing.

places.name: The Grumeti River at Kirawira
places.note: Riverine forest and the resident crocodiles, some of them enormous, with the herds bunching here for a few weeks around June. Outside that window the western corridor is a long drive for thin game.

places.name: The waterhole deck at Four Seasons Safari Lodge Serengeti
places.neighborhood: Central Serengeti, 45 minutes from Seronera airstrip
places.note: Elephants come to drink below a raised deck most afternoons in the dry months, and the bar serves non-guests. The Discovery Centre in the main building explains the migration better than most guides will.

places.name: Forodhani Gardens night market
places.note: Stalls go up at dusk along the waterfront. The pre-grilled seafood platters have been out for hours; order the Zanzibar pizza and the sugarcane juice with ginger, both made in front of you.

places.name: The Old Fort, Ngome Kongwe
places.note: Omani coral-rag walls from the 1690s around a courtyard of craft stalls and an open amphitheatre. Free to walk in, twenty minutes unless there is a taarab performance on.

places.name: House of Wonders, Beit al-Ajaib
places.note: A large part of the building collapsed during restoration in 2020 and it remains fenced with no confirmed reopening. You look at the facade and the clock tower from the gardens; do not let a guide charge you for it.

places.name: Christ Church Cathedral and the slave chambers
places.neighborhood: Mkunazini, on the old slave market site
places.note: Built over the whipping post of East Africa's last open slave market, with two holding cells preserved underneath. The cells are low, airless and the honest centre of a visit here; Sunday mornings the cathedral is in use for services.

places.name: Darajani Market
places.neighborhood: Creek Road, eastern edge of the old town
places.note: Fish, spices, fruit and a butchery section that will end your appetite. Before 09:00 it is a working market; by noon it is mostly touts.

places.name: Palace Museum, Beit el-Sahel
places.note: The Sultans' residence, with Princess Salme's rooms the reason to go. It has closed for works more than once in recent years, so have someone check it is open before you build a morning on it.

places.name: The Old Dispensary, Ithnashiri
places.note: Carved wooden balconies, stained glass and a courtyard, built as a hospital for the poor in the 1890s by an Ismaili merchant. The best-restored building on the waterfront and usually almost empty.

places.name: Emerson Spice Tea House rooftop
places.note: A five-course Swahili set menu on the highest rooftop in the old town, served cross-legged at low tables at sunset. One sitting a night, book at least two days ahead, and there is no lift.

places.name: Lukmaan Restaurant
places.note: Point at trays of pilau, octopus curry, urojo and cassava and eat for under USD 8. Locals, office workers and the occasional traveller, no ceremony, and the best value meal in Zanzibar.

places.name: 6 Degrees South rooftop
places.note: Rooftop bar over the water for the sunset hour, grilled octopus if you stay for food. Zanzibar is majority Muslim and alcohol is served in hotels and licensed places like this one rather than openly.

places.name: A Kizimbani spice farm morning
places.note: Clove, nutmeg, cinnamon bark and lemongrass pulled up in front of you, with a fruit tasting and lunch at the end. Deeply packaged, still genuinely informative, and USD 20 to 30 including transport.

places.name: Changuu, Prison Island
places.neighborhood: 30 minutes by boat northwest of Stone Town
places.note: A quarantine station that never held prisoners, and a pen of Aldabra giant tortoises, some over a century old. Around USD 4 landing fee plus the boat; go early, because by 11:00 every hotel tour is on the same beach.

places.name: Paje beach at low tide
places.note: The tide here goes out for a kilometre and comes back over hot flats, which means swimming happens on a schedule. Check the tide table the day you arrive and plan the week around it.

places.name: Kite Centre Zanzibar, Paje
places.note: Flat water inside the reef and steady side-onshore wind make this the main kite school coast in East Africa. Reliable wind is roughly June to September and December to February; outside those months lessons are a gamble.

places.name: The Rock Restaurant
places.note: A small building on a coral outcrop you wade or are rowed out to depending on the tide. The seafood is fine rather than remarkable and the bill is among the highest on the island; book weeks ahead.

places.name: Kuza Cave, Jambiani
places.neighborhood: Jambiani, inland from the beach road
places.note: A freshwater coral cave you can swim in, run as a Swahili cultural centre with drumming and cooking classes attached. Around USD 10 to swim; go at midday when the light drops through the sinkhole.

places.name: The Jambiani seaweed flats at low tide
places.note: Women farming seaweed on lines across the lagoon, which is one of the few village industries here that is not tourism. Walk out on the exposed flats, ask before photographing anyone, and wear something on your feet.

places.name: Jozani Chwaka Bay National Park
places.note: The only place the Zanzibar red colobus lives, and they sit in trees three metres from the path. About USD 10 including a compulsory guide; be there by 08:30 and do the mangrove boardwalk, which most groups skip.

places.name: Kae Funk, Michamvi Kae
places.neighborhood: Michamvi Kae, on the western side of the peninsula
places.note: The east coast faces the sunrise, so this bar on the far side of the Michamvi peninsula is where people drive for the sunset. Beanbags, reggae, cocktails, and a 30 minute road back in the dark.

places.name: Mr Kahawa, Paje
places.neighborhood: Paje village, on the beach road
places.note: Proper espresso, breakfast and shade in a village where most places serve instant. It is where the kite instructors eat before the wind fills in.

places.name: Kizimkazi Dimbani and the dolphin boats
places.note: The dolphin tours chase resident pods with a dozen boats and people jumping in on top of them, which is bad for the animals and often disappointing anyway. The 12th century Dimbani mosque, the oldest surviving Islamic building in East Africa, is the better reason to make the drive.

places.name: Mtende Beach
places.note: A small cove between coral cliffs with a village access fee of a couple of dollars, far quieter than Paje. Starfish on the rocks at low tide and one cliff-top shack selling lunch.
